The root cause is a state asymmetry: **WAL recovery replays documents into memory but never re-attaches a live WAL handle, and `SegmentImpl::flush()` uses \"live WAL handle with records\" as its only test for \"there is unpersisted data\" — so the flush inside `optimize()`'s segment switch is a silent no-op that returns OK, while the version manifest is durably rewritten to declare the segment persisted.**\n\n## 1. Recovery path vs. ordinary insertion path\n\n**Ordinary insertion** (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:903–989`): every public write (`Insert/Update/Upsert/Delete`) calls `append_wal(doc)` *before* `internal_insert/...`. `append_wal` (`segment.cc:4324–4340`) lazily calls `open_wal_file()` (`segment.cc:4303–4322`) when `wal_file_` is null. So any segment that accepted a write **in this process** has `wal_file_ != nullptr`, and the file grows past its 64-byte header (`local_wal_file.h:75–77`, `has_record()` = `file_.size() > sizeof(header_)`).\n\n**Recovery path**: `CollectionImpl::recovery()` (`src/db/collection.cc:1836–1892`) opens the writing segment, and `SegmentImpl::Open` calls `recover()` when the meta has a writing forward block (`segment.cc:484–510`). `SegmentImpl::recover()` (`segment.cc:4193–4301`):\n\n- opens the WAL through a **separate local handle** `recover_wal_file` (4206–4214), closed by `AILEGO_DEFER` (4215) — it is never assigned to the member `wal_file_`;\n- replays each record via `internal_insert/internal_update/internal_upsert/internal_delete` **directly** (4250–4266), bypassing `append_wal`.\n\n`internal_insert` (`segment.cc:837–881`) populates `id_map_` (853), `memory_store_` (857), scalar/FTS/vector in-memory indexers (861–872; vectors go to `memory_vector_indexers_`, `segment.cc:763`), the writing-block meta counters (874–876), and `doc_ids_` (878). **That is why the recovered data is immediately readable**: `Stats()` sums `segment->doc_count()` (`collection.cc:403–442`), which is `doc_ids_.size()` minus deletes (`segment.cc:589–599`), and fetch/query read `memory_store_` and the memory indexers.\n\nThe decisive difference: after recovery the segment holds N docs in memory, an N-record WAL file on disk, and **`wal_file_ == nullptr`** — the segment is blind to its own pending state.\n\n## 2.
